title: new-era-world-heavyweight
label: Larry Tact

won.source: The federation's own founding show (5 April 2004) staked its main event, a Fatal Fourway Battle Royal, as deciding "who will have the honor of being the first New ERA of Wrestling WORLD CHAMPION"; a later card (28 June 2009) confirms in its own preview text that Larry Tact became New ERA's first World Heavyweight Champion "five years and two months" earlier, dating to this same show.

note: No results thread survives naming the fourway's own winner directly; a 2009 card's own retrospective is the only document that names Larry Tact's own title win. No loss date is established in the held record; a later card (15 January 2005) already bills Jean Rabesque as champion, and a 2009 card bills Larry Tact again as a co-champion after a merger, leaving the chain between them an honest gap.

title: new-era-world-heavyweight
label: The Phantom Republican

won.source: New ERA of Wrestling's own RAUCOUS broadcast (taped 19 September 2005, aired 4 January 2006; the show's own on-screen EPISODE heading reads RAUCOUS 22): in the main event the Phantom Republican pins the champion Jean Rabesque with a sunset flip and a handful of tights, after the Masked Man walks down the ramp and Rabesque abandons an almost-locked Figure Four to shout at him. Carl Jacobs announces the result on air: "Ladies and gentlemen .... The winner of this match ....... and NEW WORLD HEAVYWEIGHT CHAMPION......... THE PHANTOM REPUBLICAN", and Tom Gheorghe closes the broadcast with "Phantom Republican ... is the World Heavyweight champion". The 12 January 2006 RAUCOUS card from which this reign's own start was previously inferred is the first captured card to follow this broadcast's own air date of 4 January 2006, and bills the same man champion.

note: The title-change match is recorded directly: New ERA's own RAUCOUS of 19 September 2005, aired 4 January 2006, in which the Phantom Republican pins Jean Rabesque with a sunset flip and a handful of tights while the Masked Man distracts the champion from the ramp (see won.source). The 12 January 2006 card's own retrospective line about ending Jean Rabesque's "year plus long reign" refers back to this same match rather than to a second one. The reign ends on the 5 July 2006 RAUCOUS, when Jonathan Marx wins the title in a Texas Tornado Tag Team match.

lost.source: New ERA of Wrestling's own RAUCOUS broadcast (taped 5 July 2006): in a Texas Tornado Tag Team match Jonathan Marx makes Beau Michaels submit to the Marxism while the Phantom Republican is caught in the ropes, and Marx is announced the new World Heavyweight Champion.

title: new-era-television
label: Jean Rabesque

won.source: The RAUCOUS 06 mirror recap (held show, enrichment-only, not served): Jean Rabesque pins John Doe in the Television Championship tournament final, and Carl Jacobs crowns him "the first New ERA TELEVISION CHAMPION" on air.

note: Numbered r002 rather than r001 because r001 (MWG, won 2005-06-20) is already held; this reign and r003 (Chaos) both precede r001 chronologically and the three may need renumbering to run in date order. Lost the title to Chaos on 2004-06-05 (see new-era-raucous-2004-06-05).

title: new-era-world-tag-team
label: Cameron Cruise & Problem Child

won.source: WFW:NE's own Destrucity II pay-per-view (23 January 2010) bills the pair champions defending against Jack n' Hoff; no earlier document in this corpus's own read slice names how or when they won the title.

title: new-era-pcx
label: Chaos

won.source: New ERA of Wrestling's own International Intrigue pay-per-view (taped 20 June 2005, aired 5 September 2005, held show, enrichment-only, not served): the PRODIGY Classic Xtreme Championship tournament final, a Tables, Ladders and Chairs match in which the belt is winched fifteen feet above the ring and the only way to win is to climb to it. Chaos beats Dallas Carter, climbing the one working ladder after a Chaos Bomb off the top rope through a table bridged between two ladders. Carl Jacobs announces the result on air: "the winner of the match ... and the first ever New ERA PRODIGY CLASSIC(C) XTREME CHAMPION.......... CHAOS!" The same broadcast's own opening commentary establishes the title as new and vacant, created by Juliet Marceau's own 27 January 2005 RAPTURE announcement in honour of the old PRODIGY circuit where New ERA's founders started, and filled by a four-man tournament.

note: The FIRST reign of this title: the belt is crowned here, not merely defended. The chain into the tournament, all from the federation's own broadcasts: Chaos beats the Sinner in an Exploding Turnbuckles first-round match (17 February 2005 RAUCOUS); Marcus LaRoque fills the other three semifinal places from the final three of that same night's ten-man Newcomer Battle Royal, won by Rex Reynolds over Dallas Carter and Thomas Lombardi; Chaos then beats Thomas Lombardi in a Taipei Death Match on the RAPTURE whose own tape date is 28 May 2005, and Dallas Carter beats Rex Reynolds in a Buried Alive match on the 30 May 2005 RAUCOUS. The federation's own 19 September 2005 RAUCOUS still bills Chaos champion and has John Doe beat him in a non-title Falls Count Anywhere match to earn a shot at the belt; Doe wins the belt from him in a Leather Strap match on the 12 January 2006 RAUCOUS.

lost.source: New ERA of Wrestling's own RAUCOUS broadcast of 12 January 2006: John Doe beats Chaos in a Leather Strap match and is announced 'NEW PRODIGY CLASSIC XTREME CHAMPION'.

title: new-era-world-heavyweight
label: Jonathan Marx

won.source: New ERA of Wrestling's own RAUCOUS broadcast (taped 5 July 2006, aired 16 July 2006; on-screen RAUCOUS 25): in a Texas Tornado Tag Team match where a fall on either man of the champion's team wins the title, Jonathan Marx makes the Phantom Republican's partner Beau Michaels submit to the Marxism while the champion hangs in the ropes. Carl Jacobs announces ‘Your NEW WORLD HEAVYWEIGHT CHAMPION … ‘GENTLEMAN’ … JONATHAN MARX!’.

lost.source: New ERA of Wrestling's own RAUCOUS broadcast (taped 19 December 2006): Shawn Hart makes Marx's arm fall three times in the Fujiwara armbar in an impromptu title match, after John Doe and Jean Rabesque turn on him.

note: He retains over the Phantom Republican by submission at BattleBRAWL 2 (19 September 2006).

won.source: New ERA of Wrestling's own RAUCOUS broadcast (taped 19 December 2006, aired 22 December 2006; on-screen RAUCOUS 27): the contract Jonathan Marx signs at a contract signing is for a title match that night, and Shawn Hart, the BattleBRAWL 2 rumble winner, wins with the Fujiwara armbar. Carl Jacobs announces him the new World Heavyweight Champion, Shawn Jessica Hart, PhD.

lost.source: New ERA of Wrestling's own RAUCOUS broadcast (taped 31 December 2006): in a shopping-mall FAO Schwartz match Luster powerbombs Hart and drags Jonathan Marx over him for the three count.

title: new-era-world-heavyweight
label: Jonathan Marx

won.source: New ERA of Wrestling's own RAUCOUS broadcast (taped 31 December 2006, aired 15 January 2007; on-screen RAUCOUS 28): Jonathan Marx pins Shawn Hart in the FAO Schwartz Match, Dominican Style, after Luster's powerbomb on Hart, and regains the title; the commentary calls him the first man to hold it twice.

note: This is Marx's second reign. The end of the reign is not established in the broadcasts read for this entry.

title: new-era-world-heavyweight
label: Shawn Hart

won.source: WFW:NE's own Unplugged card (18 July 2009) bills Larry Tact and Shawn Jessica Hart, PhD, both World Heavyweight Champion entering a stated unification match between them, the card's own main event; the following Destrucity II card (23 January 2010) bills Hart alone as champion.

note: No results document records the unification match's own outcome directly; the win is inferred from the following card's own billing. The co-championship this reign resolves is itself only attested by billing: a 28 June 2009 RAUCOUS card names Rocko Daymon and Larry Tact co-champions, and by 18 July 2009 the co-champion positions had shifted to Tact and Hart; no document in the held record explains the change between the two pairings.

title: new-era-world-heavyweight
label: The First

won.source: New ERA of Wrestling's own BattleBRAWL 3 card (20 March 2011) already bills The First champion, entering a defense against a rival whose own promo on the same card states he took the belt from that rival directly; New ERA's own Cyberstrike 02 lineup (8 February 2011, read but not served) still billed that same rival champion six weeks earlier, bounding the change to within that window.

note: The exact date and event of this title change are not captured in the held record; the previous documented champions were 2009's co-titleholders. New ERA's own rules document (dated 15 January 2011 in its own text) separately states its reigning World Heavyweight Champion "became" the first champion under this renamed title at the same transition, without naming him.

title: new-era-television
label: Chaos

won.source: New ERA of Wrestling's own RAUCOUS broadcast of 5 June 2004: an unidentified person dressed all in black comes through the crowd, superkicks Jean Rabesque and drags Chaos on top of him for the pinfall that wins the Television Championship.

note: Numbered r003 rather than r001 or r002 because r001 (MWG, won 2005-06-20) is already held and r002 (Jean Rabesque) precedes this reign; the three may need renumbering to run in date order. No loss date is established in the read documents; a later card (17 September 2005) already bills MWG champion, leaving the chain between them an honest gap.

title: new-era-television
label: Suicide

won.source: New ERA of Wrestling's own Destrucity pay-per-view (6 July 2004): wrestling under a mask as Spectre, he wins the Electrified Exploding Cage match for the Television Championship from Chaos, then unmasks as Suicide, revealed never to have left the promotion.

note: Numbered r004 rather than r001 because r001 (MWG, won 2005-06-20) is already held and r002 (Jean Rabesque) and r003 (Chaos) precede it chronologically; r002 through r005 all predate r001, and the whole chain runs out of date order pending a titles/reigns renumbering correction. Vacated on the 6 August 2004 RAUCOUS after Suicide's own reported car accident; New ERA of Wrestling's own BattleBRAWL pay-per-view (3 December 2004) shows MWG winning the vacant title in the event's own battle royal, but no reign row for that win exists yet in this wing's own shard.

title: new-era-television
label: Alex Borden

won.source: New ERA of Wrestling's own RAUCOUS broadcast of 6 August 2004: he wins the vacant Television Championship in a triple threat over MWG and John Doe.

note: Numbered r005 for the same reason as r004 above; the whole r002-r005 chain predates the held r001 and needs renumbering into date order. Stripped on the 28 September 2004 RAUCOUS after going AWOL from the promotion; the title stood vacant into BattleBRAWL, where MWG wins it in the event's own battle royal (see r004's own note).

title: new-era-television
label: MWG

won.source: New ERA of Wrestling's own BattleBRAWL pay-per-view (3 December 2004, held show, enrichment-only, not served): MWG, the #1 contender since Alex Borden's stripping, enters last in the over-the-top BattleBRAWL Rumble and eliminates the final two men, Cameron Cruise and Jason Payne, together with a running knee lift. Carl Jacobs announces him on air as "the recipient of the FIRST EVER BattleBRAWL Championship Cup ... as WELL as the NEW ERA of WRESTLING TELEVISION CHAMPION." The broadcast's own pre-match commentary establishes the vacant title (stripped from Alex Borden on the 28 September 2004 RAUCOUS) was on the line, awarded to the rumble's own winner.

note: This is MWG's FIRST New ERA Television Championship reign; his second (already held as r001, won 20 June 2005 at International Intrigue) is a separate, later reign of the same title after it sat vacant for several months — see the correction to r001 in reigns-corrections-new-era-of-wrestling.json. This reign is numbered r006 rather than by date order to avoid an id collision with r002-r005, which are already assigned to the earlier reigns in this chain. True chronological order of the title's reigns to date: Jean Rabesque (r002, won 2004-04-05) -> Chaos (r003, won 2004-06-05) -> Suicide (r004, won 2004-07-06) -> Alex Borden (r005, won 2004-08-06) -> MWG's first reign (r006, this row, won 2004-12-03) -> MWG's second reign (r001, won 2005-06-20).

lost.source: New ERA of Wrestling's own RAUCOUS broadcast (taped 29 January 2005; the show's own on-screen EPISODE heading reads RAUCOUS 19): defending against Jason Payne, Payne reverses MWG's go-behind into a bridging German suplex that pins both men's shoulders to the mat simultaneously. The referee rules the title cannot be awarded to either man ("the referee isn't awarding the title to EITHER competitor"), and it sits vacant. New ERA's own International Intrigue broadcast (20 June 2005) recaps this directly: "The championship was held in limbo the past few months, due to a spectacular match between Madonna Wayne Grossard and Jason Payne that ended in a draw."

title: new-era-television
label: MWG

won.source: New ERA of Wrestling's own International Intrigue pay-per-view (taped 20 June 2005): in a Blood Frenzy Dance Party Death Match, MWG defeats Jason Payne for the vacant Television Championship (Krist Blue's own interference saves MWG from a Payne near-fall by putting his foot on the ropes; MWG finishes with a Disappear Here DDT onto a chemical-soaked chair). Carl Jacobs announces the result on air: "the winner of the match .... and the NEW ERA OF WRESTLING TELEVISION CHAMPION ..... EM DUBBYA GEE!" The federation's own following RAPTURE card (taped 17 September 2005) confirms this is MWG's own FIRST DEFENSE of this reign (on-air: "MWG in his first title defense from decisively winning the title that he should have never lost") and he retains there against Mr. Entertainment.

note: A results document does name MWG the winner at International Intrigue directly (see won.source). This is MWG's SECOND New ERA Television Championship reign. Mr. Entertainment takes the title from him in a Marco Polo blindfold match on the 5 July 2006 RAUCOUS. The title's next recorded champion, Cameron Cruise, is billed on a card of 23 January 2010 (Destrucity II).

lost.source: New ERA of Wrestling's own RAUCOUS broadcast (taped 5 July 2006): Mr. Entertainment pins MWG in a Marco Polo blindfold match and is announced the new Television Champion.

won.source: New ERA of Wrestling's own RAUCOUS broadcast of 12 January 2006: in a Leather Strap match John Doe beats the champion Chaos, and Carl Jacobs announces 'NEW PRODIGY CLASSIC XTREME CHAMPION ... JOHN DOE!'; the commentary calls it DREDD's first title victory in New ERA. The match follows his Falls Count Anywhere win over Chaos on the 19 September 2005 RAUCOUS.

lost.source: New ERA of Wrestling's own RAUCOUS broadcast (taped 3 February 2006): Doe defends in a Scaffold and Tables match against Chaos and Trevor Cane, and Chaos Chaosbombs him from the scaffold through burning tables and is announced 'NEW PRODIGY© CLASSIC XTREME CHAMPION'.

title: new-era-womens-heavyweight
label: Karla Starr

won.source: New ERA of Wrestling's own RAUCOUS broadcast of 5 July 2006: Tom Gheorghe says Karla Starr won the Women's title at the first BattleBRAWL by cheating Caitlyn Daymon out of a hard-fought victory, after Starr went through four other women in the Spin the Wheel, Make the Deal gauntlet match. Juliet Marceau's own speech on the 19 December 2006 RAUCOUS puts that night at ‘December 3, 2004’, ‘BattleBRAWL in Seattle, Washington’, where New ERA ‘crowned its first ever Women’s champion’.

lost.source: New ERA of Wrestling's own RAUCOUS broadcast (taped 19 December 2006): Juliet Marceau announces ‘The New ERA’s Women championship … IS OVER’ and Karla Starr takes the faceplate off the belt to show the VENUS World Heavyweight Championship plate underneath, making her ‘the FIRST VENUS World Heavyweight champion’.

note: The whole of this title's run is the one reign. The BattleBRAWL 2 pay-per-view (19 September 2006) has Starr retain over Foxx, and the broadcasts of 2006 show her defending it or putting it up against her challengers; its video package dates her win 19 December 2004 where Marceau and the BattleBRAWL card give 3 December. The same belt carries on as the VENUS World Heavyweight Championship.

title: new-era-pcx
label: Chaos

won.source: New ERA of Wrestling's own RAUCOUS broadcast (taped 3 February 2006, aired 27 June 2006; the show's own on-screen EPISODE heading reads RAUCOUS 24): after forcing Marcus LaRoque to change the match to a Scaffold and Tables match as a condition of re-signing, Chaos wins at 21:39 when he blinds John Doe with lighter fluid, sets the tables below on fire and Chaosbombs him through them. Carl Jacobs announces him the new PRODIGY© Classic Xtreme Champion.

The belt stays on him through all of them.

title: new-era-world-heavyweight
label: The First

won.source: New ERA of Wrestling's own Cyberstrike 12 card (12 August 2011) bills Fanatic defending against The First in the main event; New ERA's own Cyberstrike 13 lineup (25 August 2011, read but not served) bills The First champion two weeks later. The First remains billed champion at BANNED in the US II (6 April 2015), defending against a wrestler cashing in a banked shot; his own roster bio card independently records two New ERA Championship reigns, matching this and his earlier r004 reign.

note: The First's title status between Cyberstrike 13 (25 August 2011) and BANNED in the US II (6 April 2015) is not captured in the held record, which carries no documents dated between the federation's own 2011 hiatus and its March 2015 return; whether he held the belt continuously or regained it during the unread gap is an honest open question. BANNED in the US II's own results are not captured, so whether he retained here is likewise unresolved.
